summary: Name the resolved loop.pid path in the `status` and `loop` EX_IOERR refusals, as their stop-flag and merging-dir siblings already do

per.section: Narration is the ladder's bottom rung

acceptance: Both arms print the lock path the verb resolved, and the comment asserting the I/O error carries it is gone — shrunk to what the message now holds.
tests: flume loop refuses an unreadable loop.pid naming the resolved lock path
flume status refuses an unreadable loop.pid naming the resolved lock path
notes: Measured while driving loop's three 74 arms: node's EISDIR from reading a directory carries no path, so the operator gets `loop.pid failed to read: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read` — a state-root-relative name under a root that may be relocated. Both call sites already hold the path (`loopLockPath(flumeDir)`). Sibling shape is `<thing> at ${path} failed to ...`. The tick-verdicts arms name-only too, but carry no such claim; out of scope.
